projectBackground.name: Year-End Financial Statements — Harbour Components Ltd
projectBackground.timeline: Statements due to auditors in 10 working days
projectBackground.context: Harbour's draft accounts contain unadjusted inventory, an asset register without depreciation, and a revenue contract spanning year-end.

manager.name: Priya Nair
manager.note: Auditors will test every adjustment against the standard. Show me which IFRS you're applying, the calculation, and why it is the right treatment.

assignment.title: Adjust the draft accounts and interpret the ratios
assignment.brief: Apply IAS 2, IAS 16 and IFRS 15 correctly, compute liquidity ratios in Excel for three clients and explain the write-down to the board.

documents.name: Draft Statement of Financial Position
documents.note: Inventory carried at cost £120,000; estimated net realisable value £105,000.

documents.name: Fixed Asset Register
documents.note: Machine cost £250,000; residual £25,000; useful life 5 years; purchased two years ago.

documents.name: Revenue Contract Summary
documents.note: Multi-period service contract with performance obligations delivered over time.

tasks.title: Inventory Valuation
tasks.prompt: Under IAS 2, inventory must be measured at:
options: The lower of cost and net realisable value
tasks.reasoning: IAS 2 prevents assets being overstated: if NRV is below cost, inventory is written down.
tasks.tip: Compare cost to NRV item by item, not on the total unless items are similar.
tasks.mistake: Carrying inventory at cost when NRV is lower overstates profit and assets.
tasks.recommendation: Write down your reasoning and the evidence behind it so a reviewer can verify your conclusion quickly.

tasks.title: Inventory Write-Down
tasks.prompt: Inventory cost is £120,000 and net realisable value is £105,000. What write-down must be recognised?
tasks.reasoning: The £15,000 difference reduces inventory to NRV and is charged to profit.
tasks.tip: Recognise write-downs in the period they occur.
tasks.mistake: Waiting for the item to sell defers a known loss.
tasks.recommendation: Write down your reasoning and the evidence behind it so a reviewer can verify your conclusion quickly.

tasks.title: Net Book Value
tasks.prompt: A machine cost £250,000 with residual value £25,000 and a five-year life (straight-line). What is its net book value after two years?
tasks.workingNote: Annual depreciation = (250,000 - 25,000) / 5 = 45,000. After two years accumulated = 90,000. NBV = 160,000.
tasks.reasoning: Depreciation is based on depreciable amount (cost less residual), not full cost.
tasks.tip: Subtract the residual value before dividing by the useful life.
tasks.mistake: Using full cost gives £50,000 per year and an NBV of £150,000 — wrong.
tasks.recommendation: Write down your reasoning and the evidence behind it so a reviewer can verify your conclusion quickly.

tasks.title: Revenue Recognition
tasks.prompt: Under IFRS 15, revenue on a service delivered over time is recognised when:
options: Performance obligations are satisfied, over the period the service is provided
tasks.reasoning: IFRS 15 ties revenue to transfer of control, not to cash or billing.
tasks.mistake: Recognising on invoice timing misstates revenue in the wrong period.
tasks.recommendation: Write down your reasoning and the evidence behind it so a reviewer can verify your conclusion quickly.

tasks.title: Cash Flow Adjustments
tasks.prompt: Using the indirect method, select the items that adjust profit to arrive at operating cash flow.
options: Deduct dividends paid as an operating item
Add the proceeds of a share issue
tasks.reasoning: Non-cash charges and working-capital movements adjust profit to cash from operations; financing flows are shown separately.
tasks.tip: Ask: is it non-cash or a working-capital movement?
tasks.mistake: Mixing financing items into operating cash distorts the statement.
tasks.recommendation: Write down your reasoning and the evidence behind it so a reviewer can verify your conclusion quickly.

tasks.title: Liquidity Ratios (Excel)
tasks.prompt: Complete current ratio (E = B / D) and quick ratio (F = (B - C) / D) for three clients. Upload for checking.
tasks.reasoning: Quick ratio excludes inventory because it is the least liquid current asset.
tasks.tip: Use cell references so ratios update if figures change.
tasks.mistake: Copying inventory into the quick ratio overstates liquidity.
tasks.recommendation: Write down your reasoning and the evidence behind it so a reviewer can verify your conclusion quickly.

tasks.title: Board Explanation
tasks.prompt: Explain to the board in 3-4 sentences why the £15,000 inventory write-down is required and what it does to profit.
tasks.modelAnswer: Under IAS 2, inventory must not be carried above the amount we expect to recover. The stock cost £120,000 but can only be sold for £105,000 net, so we recognise a £15,000 write-down this year. This reduces reported profit by £15,000 but prevents overstating assets and gives the auditors a defensible number. It also signals a pricing or obsolescence issue that management should review.
tasks.reasoning: A good explanation cites the standard, the calculation and the business implication.
tasks.tip: Link the accounting to the business reason.
tasks.mistake: Citing a rule without showing the numbers invites audit challenge.
tasks.recommendation: Write down your reasoning and the evidence behind it so a reviewer can verify your conclusion quickly.

caseStudy.title: Case Study: The Overstated Stock
caseStudy.background: A manufacturer carried obsolete stock at cost for three years. When the auditor tested NRV the write-down was £480,000 and wiped out half of the year's profit.
caseStudy.challenges: Management assumed slow-moving stock would eventually sell at full price.
caseStudy.constraints: No NRV review was performed during the year.
questions: Why is deferring a known loss misleading?
What routine would have found the issue earlier?
How should obsolete items be flagged?
caseStudy.solution: Ledger & Co. introduced a quarterly NRV review with an ageing report and sign-off by the finance director.
caseStudy.lessonsLearned: Review NRV regularly; obsolescence is a recurring risk, not a year-end surprise.
